title: Build a dead man's switch for your business with an agent
summary: A solo web studio owner had Claude Code build a self-hosted check-in system from a detailed spec; it alerts next of kin, then clients, if he goes silent.
agent_role: Claude Code wrote the software from the owner's long written spec, and it passed 42 automatic tests. The owner designed the plan, set it up and tested it on himself.
outcome: Author reports running it on himself for weeks and says clients see it as a strong sales feature.
what_they_did: Peter Bishop runs a one-person web studio and wanted a plan in case he dies or goes missing. He wrote a detailed spec and had Claude Code build the tool. It emails him weekly. If he doesn't press the check-in button, it asks his next of kin first. Only then does it send his prepared messages to other contacts.
how_it_went: He says the code passed 42 automatic tests and he has been running it on himself. He reports clients like it when they trust him with their accounts.
worth_knowing: It only sends emails and stores no passwords. It should run on hosting separate from the sites it protects, so one outage can't take down both.
prompt: Build a small self-hosted check-in tool for my business. Every week at [day and time] it should email me a check-in button. If I don't press it, send reminders at 24 and 48 hours. Then ask [next of kin email] whether I'm all right. If they say something is wrong or don't reply within [days], email each contact in [contact list] their own prepared message. Opening a link must not count as checking in. Write automatic tests, show me the plan first, and don't send any real emails until I approve.

curation.rationale: A useful, original small-business tool built with Claude Code from a written spec, with code released. Details on what the agent did are thin.
